solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: False part of argument by those in favour

indicators.note: by means next to, so the argument stands beside the supporters' word

parts.note: pros are those for something, as in pros and cons
a thesis is a proposition argued for

explanation.surface: A debating point is dismissed as a false part of the case made by its supporters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'False part' looks like a criticism of the argument, but it defines an artificial body part.
explanation.definitionFit: A prosthesis is an artificial replacement for a missing limb or other body part.

clue.text: Drive from hospital after discharge

indicators.note: after means the hospital letter comes behind the word for discharge

parts.note: pus is matter discharged from an infection

explanation.surface: A patient is driven away from hospital after being discharged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discharge' looks like being let out of hospital, but it is matter oozing from a wound.
explanation.definitionFit: Drive and push both mean to press forward or propel, and also determination.

clue.text: Outstanding feud revolutionary suppresses during rising

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means reading upwards, so the concealed letters run backwards
suppresses means holds down or conceals, so the letters are concealed within the words

explanation.surface: A rebel crushes a feud while an uprising is going on.
explanation.walkthrough: The concealed run is EUDREVO, spanning 'feud' and 'revolutionary', which 'rising' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: Outstanding in the sense of still unpaid or not yet done means late or past its due date.

clue.text: Newspaper survey reported support for pre-wireless communications

parts.note: the Telegraph is a British daily newspaper, the one that publishes this puzzle

indicators.note: reported means said or spoken, so the word for survey is heard rather than written

parts.note: a poll is a survey of opinion

explanation.surface: A newspaper's survey is reported to back old-fashioned communications.
explanation.walkthrough: A nod to the setter's own paper, the Daily Telegraph.
explanation.definitionFit: Telegraph wires before radio were strung between tall wooden posts carrying the lines.

clue.text: Toothless old prime minister installed as head of state

indicators.note: installed as head of means the old leader's name replaces the first letter of the word state

parts.note: Anthony Eden was British prime minister in the 1950s

explanation.surface: A former premier is sworn in as head of state, yet has no teeth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Toothless' looks like a jibe at a powerless leader, but it is the definition, as in the zoological order of anteaters and sloths.
explanation.definitionFit: Edentate is a zoological term for lacking teeth, from Latin e- (out) and dens (tooth).

clue.text: Force politician into convoluted lie

indicators.note: into means the politician goes inside the twisted letters
convoluted means twisted, so the word lie is twisted into another order

parts.note: MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A politician is forced into a tangled lie.
explanation.definitionFit: To impel is to drive or compel someone to act.

clue.text: Settler succeeded in the modern age

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for succeeded, as used in family trees
now is the present time

explanation.surface: A historical note that some pioneer took over a homestead in recent times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Settler' looks like a colonist, but it is what settles: lying snow is said to settle.
explanation.definitionFit: Falling flakes that stay on the ground are said to settle, so a whimsical word for them is something that settles.

clue.text: I will get stuck into refried Chinese — mostly quite good

indicators.note: to get stuck into is to be pushed inside, so the letter I goes among the reworked letters
refried means cooked again, so the remaining letters are churned into a new order
mostly means all but the last letter of the word Chinese is used

explanation.surface: Someone tucks into reheated Chinese takeaway and pronounces it fairly decent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'refried' works on CHINES (Chinese without its last E), giving NICESH, and I is put inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Niceish is a casual word for fairly pleasant or reasonably satisfactory.

clue.text: Fierce eastern insects beginning to taunt antelope

parts.note: wild means savage or fierce
bees are insects

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, here that of taunt

explanation.surface: Savage swarming insects start tormenting a grazing antelope.
explanation.definitionFit: The wildebeest, or gnu, is a large African antelope known for its mass migrations.

clue.text: Time to get letters in order

definitions.meaning: a stretch of time, as in a ... of fine weather
to give the letters of a word in their correct sequence

explanation.surface: Someone is told it is time to sort out their correspondence.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a period of time and to name the letters of a word one by one.

clue.text: Pal and I dabbled with crime, as established by trial

indicators.note: to dabble is to mess about with, so the letters of the words are messed about into a new order

explanation.surface: A confession that two friends dabbled in crime, as was proved in court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'established by trial' reads as a court verdict, but defines knowledge gained by experiment.
explanation.definitionFit: Empirical knowledge rests on observation and experiment rather than theory.

clue.text: Order for starters prepared today with eggs half-heartedly scrambled

parts.note: ready means prepared

indicators.note: scrambled eggs are mixed up, so these letters are mixed into a new order
half-heartedly means half of the middle of the word eggs is lost, one of its two central letters

explanation.surface: A breakfast order: starters are ready and today's eggs come scrambled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starters' looks like first courses but means those starting a race; the anagram of TODAY and EGS gives STEADY GO.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the traditional command given to start children's races.

clue.text: Millennial figure's unworldly — time to intervene

parts.note: of a figure, that is relating to numerical digits

indicators.note: to intervene is to come between, so the short time letter goes in among the letters of the word for unworldly

parts.note: naive means innocent of the world's ways

explanation.surface: A sneer that some young celebrity is naive and it is time someone stepped in.
explanation.walkthrough: DIGITAL is taken from 'figure's' in the sense of belonging to figures, that is numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: A digital native is someone of the generation raised with the internet, as millennials were.

clue.text: Latin American actor with ego has ability

parts.note: a co-star is a fellow actor sharing top billing
ego is Latin for I
can means is able to

explanation.surface: A self-centred actor from Latin America is said to be talented.
explanation.definitionFit: Costa Rica is a Central American country, so a native of it is Latin American.

clue.text: Past legislation performs badly

parts.note: over means finished, in the past
acts are laws passed by parliament

explanation.surface: Old laws are said to work badly in practice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'performs badly' looks like old laws failing, but it means hamming on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: To ham, exaggerating a role, is a theatrical sense of performing badly.

clue.text: Fruit husband brought into school

indicators.note: brought into means put inside, so the husband's letter goes into the school

parts.note: a lycée is a French secondary school

explanation.surface: A spouse carries some fruit into a school.
explanation.definitionFit: The lychee is a small sweet fruit with a rough red skin, originally from China.

clue.text: To keep bouncing ball may be such an activity?

definitions.meaning: to save from harm or decay, as fruit is kept in jars

definitions.text: bouncing ball may be such an activity?
definitions.meaning: read as ..., describing what a tennis player does before serving

explanation.surface: A question whether keeping a ball bouncing counts as some activity.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the word as PRE-SERVE: tennis players bounce the ball before they serve.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to keep or maintain, and the split form describes something done before a serve.

clue.text: Your old blankets and so on getting ratty

indicators.note: blankets means covers or wraps round, so the old word for your goes around the and-so-on abbreviation

parts.note: thy is the old form of your
etc is short for et cetera, and so on

explanation.surface: Your old blankets and the rest are getting worn and moth-eaten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ratty' looks like shabby bedding, but it means bad-tempered.
explanation.definitionFit: Ratty is British informal for irritable, a synonym of crabby or peevish.

clue.text: City lost in billowing Atlantic, one submerged as this was?

definitions.text: City lost in billowing Atlantic, one submerged as this was?

indicators.note: submerged means sunk below the surface, so the letter for one goes inside
billowing means heaving like waves, so the remaining letters are tossed into a new order
lost in means the city's letters go missing from the ocean's name

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles, the US city
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A city lost under heaving Atlantic waves, with one ship sunk like this famous liner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'billowing' reworks ATNTIC, what is left once the city goes. The whole clue also describes the liner that sank in 1912, so it is an &lit.
explanation.definitionFit: The Titanic was the liner that sank in the North Atlantic on its maiden voyage in 1912.

clue.text: Wastes food

definitions.meaning: squanders, as in frittering money away
pieces of fried battered food, such as apple or corn ones

explanation.surface: A two-word comment on throwing away good food.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means squanders, and the noun names battered fried morsels.

clue.text: The Spanish say member of social network is stylish

parts.note: el is Spanish for the
eg, for example, is what say means
an ant is a social insect living in a colony network

explanation.surface: A Spanish user of a social networking site is said to be stylish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'social network' suggests the internet, but it is an ant colony.
explanation.definitionFit: Elegant means graceful and refined in style or appearance.

clue.text: Ceremony for ape is stage managed?

indicators.note: the stage is managed, so its letters with the others are arranged in a new order

explanation.surface: A wry question whether a stage-managed event is a ritual meant for an ape.
explanation.walkthrough: The '?' signals that the whole clue also hints at the answer: a staged ritual.
explanation.definitionFit: A rite of passage is a ceremony marking a transition, such as initiation or coming of age.

clue.text: Edmondson perhaps breaking record during climb to cause a revolution in cycling?

definitions.text: to cause a revolution in cycling?

indicators.note: in a down clue climb means going upwards, so the letters read from the bottom
breaking means splitting open, so the comic's first name goes inside the record

parts.note: LP is a long-playing record
Ade Edmondson is a British comic actor, star of The Young Ones

explanation.surface: A comedian smashes a cycling record on a mountain climb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolution' suggests uprising but means turning the cranks round on a bicycle.
explanation.definitionFit: Pushing on a cycle's foot lever turns the cranks, causing each revolution of the wheels.

clue.text: Eager to lift foot above middle part of leg

indicators.note: in a down clue the foot is the bottom letter, which is lifted up above the letter before it

parts.note: keen means eager

explanation.surface: A keen walker lifts a foot over the middle of a leg of the route.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foot' looks like a body part, close to the answer, but it means the bottom letter of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: The knee is the joint midway down the leg, between thigh and shin.

clue.text: Tory bid to be candidate

parts.note: Con is the abbreviation for Conservative, the party also called Tory
a tender is a formal offer or bid

explanation.surface: A Conservative politician makes a bid to stand for election.
explanation.definitionFit: A contender is someone competing for a post or title, such as an election hopeful.

clue.text: Long months before November

parts.note: a year is twelve months
N is November in the radio alphabet

explanation.surface: It is a long wait of many months before November comes round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long' looks like an adjective about time, but it is the verb meaning to crave.
explanation.definitionFit: To long for something is to desire it deeply, the same as to pine or ache.

clue.text: Spoon in top of bottle

definitions.meaning: an old verb meaning to kiss and cuddle
the narrow upper part of a bottle

explanation.surface: A spoon is left in the top of a bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to kiss amorously and the narrow part of a bottle below its mouth.

clue.text: Fly low — that takes courage

parts.note: blue means sad or down in spirits
bottle is British slang for nerve or courage

explanation.surface: Flying low is said to need nerve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fly low' reads as a daredevil instruction, but 'Fly' is the noun and 'low' means sad.
explanation.definitionFit: A bluebottle is a large blowfly with a metallic blue body.
